newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Prince Salman concerned at Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Prince Salman concerned at Mideast peace.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac met Saudi Arabian Prince Salman on Wednesday and both expressed concern at the fate of the Arab-Israeli peace process, officials said.

"(Chirac) did not hide his great concern," Chirac's spokeswoman Catherine Colonna told reporters, saying the president wanted peace to be reached through solutions in line with the spirit and letter of the Oslo peace accords.
"We note that (Saudi Arabia) is equally concerned and believes like France that we must get out of the current impasse which is dangerous and may be lasting," the spokeswoman said.
The prince, brother of Saudi Arabia's King Fahd, said he supported European peace initiatives. "Who could refuse them? I don't believe any Arab could reject them," Salman said.
He said that he and Chirac had convergent views on "all questions of common interest between the two countries" as well as on international or regional questions.
Prince Salman, invited to Paris by the capital's mayor, has met Prime Minister Alain Juppe, Foreign Minister Herve de Charette and Defence Minister Charles Millon during his visit.
